metrics.reason: The staple drops the 4 mixed space-time rectangles while the action keeps them, so it stops being dS/dU. S1a/S1b are the bond-counting identity sum_links Re tr(U A) == 4 sum_loops beta Re tr P and must fail at O(1); the RIGHT-HAND SIDE of that identity deliberately keeps the full action, because dropping the mixed loops there too would make the control self-consistent and green, which is the V-004 defect class. O1a spills and is DECLARED rather than excluded: over-relaxation is microcanonical only with respect to the action its staple is the derivative of, so an incomplete staple provably cannot preserve the full S. Measured, not expected.

One colour class instead of four, so a staple is reused for links that DO share a plaquette. This is the single-legged control: everything algebraic about the construction is unchanged and only the microcanonical identity can see it, which is exactly what the checkerboard exists to protect. The bipartition being tested is a property of the BCC graph, not a convention -- a rhombus with sides {a, e} carries two a-bonds stored one hop apart, and the nearest-neighbour graph is bipartite, so leg B1b is the theorem and O1a is its consequence.

Drops the "- d" of U_{-d}(x) = U_d(x - d)^dag, i.e. the realistic off-by-one-hop bug. Nothing leaves SU(N) -- the stored fields are untouched and a product of unitaries is unitary -- so H1a and H1b CANNOT detect it, which is the reason gauge invariance is in this record at all. G1b stays GREEN and that is measured rather than expected: `_transporter` builds R x T loops from forward hops only and daggers whole legs, so the Wilson-loop path never reaches the corrupted branch. The same asymmetry is why W1a reddens -- the action's mixed rectangle is corrupted while the loop is not, so the two objects that leg asserts are identical stop agreeing.

Predict the TEXTBOOK hypercubic beta_t/beta_s = xi^2 instead of the BCC 4 lambda^2/a_t^2 = (4/3) xi^2. The measured weak-field ratio is unchanged at 4, so the prediction misses it by exactly the 4/3 this derivation supplies -- i.e. the control IS the new content, and the leg it reddens is the one that measured rather than assumed. Note what is NOT a control here: c_lat cannot be perturbed to redden anything, because changing it moves a_t and the prediction together (the derivation is self-consistent at any c_lat). The falsifiable content is the relation beta_t/beta_s = 4 lambda^2/a_t^2, and this is the control that tests it.

Build the higher reps as the raw tensor power, chi = (Tr W)^k, instead of projecting onto the symmetric subspace. This is the realistic mistake and it is precisely why the explicit-matrix cross-check exists: F299's polynomials had only ever been checked against the Jacobi-Trudi determinant that produced them, which cannot catch a wrong SYMMETRISATION because both sides would carry it. Single-legged -- K1b's dimension count is deliberately left green, since forgetting to symmetrise does not change the dimension of the matrix you built.
